page_title: Nightwatch: clear-sky planning and astrophotography targets for Mac

summary.name: Nightwatch
summary.one_liner: A free, open-source Mac menu-bar app that finds tonight's clear-sky window and ranks astrophotography targets for it, telling you when it is worth setting up a telescope.
keywords: when to image the night sky
use_cases: Deciding whether tonight is clear enough to set up a telescope
Choosing which deep-sky target to image on a given night
Getting a heads-up before sunset about a clear imaging window
Checking aurora alerts from a Mac menu bar
Planning multi-night stacks with a DWARF or Seestar telescope
summary.what_it_does:
Nightwatch runs in the Mac menu bar and checks the forecast every 30 minutes, alerting an hour before sunset only when there is a continuous dark, clear run long enough to image. The default go rule requires at least 3 hours of clear sky with 25% or less cloud (thin high cloud counts for half) and the Sun below 18 degrees (astronomical darkness); these thresholds are adjustable. It scores each night on cloud, Moon, seeing, transparency and wind, and ranks targets for the sky you can actually see, using terrain blocking that you describe for your site. Forecasts come from Apple Weather and Open-Meteo, with MET Norway and 7Timer as fallbacks, and all calculations run on the Mac.</think>
<parameter name="pricing">free
notable: Free and open source Mac menu-bar app with no account or API key, calculations done on the Mac
Presets for DwarfLab DWARF Mini, DWARF 3, Draco and ZWO Seestar S30, S30 Pro, S50, S50 Pro; any telescope can be set by field of view
Siri, Spotlight and Shortcuts integration, including a Clear Window Tonight yes/no action
Aurora alerts from AuroraWatch UK in the UK and Ireland and NOAA elsewhere
caveats: Data sources are licensed for non-commercial use, so the app is free with no ads or subscriptions
Does not control telescopes; it only advises when and what to image
Makes no claim of better forecast accuracy than its data sources
Some features depend on the latest Mac software (Siri)
